>>> When an mRNA vaccine is injected into the body, it enters the cells at the injection site.  
>>> The mRNA in the vaccine contains instructions for making a specific protein, usually a piece of the virus's spike protein.  
>>> Once inside the cells, the mRNA is taken up by the cell's machinery, specifically the ribosomes.  
>>> The ribosomes use the mRNA as a template to produce the viral protein.  
>>> The newly made viral protein is then displayed on the surface of the cell.  
>>> The immune system recognizes the foreign protein as a threat and starts an immune response.  
>>> This immune response includes the production of antibodies and activation of T-cells.  
>>> The antibodies are designed to recognize and neutralize the virus if it enters the body in the future.  
>>> The T-cells help to destroy any cells that have been infected by the virus.  
>>> After the immune response is triggered, the mRNA is broken down and cleared from the body.  
>>> The immune system retains a memory of the viral protein, allowing for a faster and more effective response if exposed to the actual virus.
